questions.question: List the five functions of the skeleton with one example or detail for each.
questions.expected_answer: Support: a rigid frame that holds the body upright. Movement: bones act as levers pulled by muscles at joints. Protection: skull protects the brain, rib cage protects the heart and lungs, vertebrae protect the spinal cord. Production of blood cells: red bone marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets. Storage: bone stores calcium and phosphate for release into the blood.

questions.question: Explain why muscles must work in antagonistic pairs, using the biceps and triceps to describe bending and straightening the elbow.
questions.expected_answer: A muscle can only pull: it contracts to shorten and then relaxes, but relaxing does not push the bone back. So a second muscle on the opposite side of the joint is needed to reverse the movement. Bending: biceps contracts, triceps relaxes, the radius is pulled up at the hinge joint of the elbow. Straightening: triceps contracts, biceps relaxes, the forearm is pulled down.

questions.question: Distinguish between tendons and ligaments, and between a fracture and a sprain, and name the three types of freely movable joint with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone and stabilise joints. A fracture is a crack or break in a bone; a sprain is damage to the ligaments of a joint forced beyond its range. Hinge joint: elbow or knee, one-plane bending. Ball-and-socket joint: shoulder or hip, movement in all directions with rotation. Pivot joint: between the first two neck vertebrae, rotation of one bone about another.
